request.spec:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Only draft claims can be edited now, and a voided claim keeps its number. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

- **Editing an open claim is refused.** I added `RefuseNonDraftEdit.java` as a step in the claim's edit endpoint (`claims/{claimId}.PUT.yml`). It runs right after the claim is loaded, so a refused edit writes nothing to the store or the audit file. The server returns "Only a DRAFT claim can be edited; void it and add a new one instead", which shows as the form's error on that claim (`claim-form-error`). The editor stays open until it's cancelled. The Edit button still appears on every claim, because the test presses it on an open claim and expects the refusal.
- **Voiding keeps the number.** `ApplyClaimStatus` no longer clears the number on void, so the row still shows it and `CLAIM_VOIDED` ends with `number=N`. Numbers still come from the sheet's counter, so they are never reused. A claim voided while still a draft never had a number, so its audit line has none.

Claims voided before this change already lost their numbers, and there's no way to get those back. I didn't add a database migration, because the table doesn't change. That leaves the comment in the existing `V8__claim_number.sql` migration out of date: it still says voiding clears the number. I left it alone because editing a migration that has already been applied can make Flyway reject it.
